title: NY State Assembly · District 87
area: Southeast Bronx, including Parkchester, Castle Hill, Van Nest, West Farms, Unionport and Westchester Square.

context.text: Incumbent Karines Reyes defeated Zakir Choudhury 71.6%-28.1% in the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary. Choudhury remains on the November ballot on the People First Party line, a separate ballot line he also secured. Zenobia Merced-Bonilla advanced unopposed on the Conservative Party line.

candidates.name: Karines Reyes

priorities.text: Affordable education: fully funding Foundation Aid for K-12 schools and passing the New Deal for CUNY to provide tuition relief.
Affordable housing: protecting tenants and holding negligent landlords accountable.
Affordable healthcare: pushing for a healthcare system that works for patients over insurance companies.
Immigration justice: legislation to give immigrant residents stability, dignity and a fair shot.

positions.summary: In her 2020 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey she listed passing the New York Health Act, universal health care, as a campaign message.
positions.quote: Universal Health Care - Pass the New York Health Act

positions.summary: Says she works to protect tenants and hold negligent landlords accountable, and to push Albany to invest in housing that keeps working families in place.

Says she leads the fight for the New York for All Act to protect immigrants regardless of status; in an April 2026 statement with State Senator Andrew Gounardes she said the act would ban all collusion with ICE.
positions.quote: Our New York For All Act would ban all collusion with ICE and truly protect New Yorkers’ civil rights, including due process.

positions.summary: Says she championed Abortion Shield Laws protecting doctors and patients involved in abortion care.
In her 2020 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey she listed progressive taxation, including raising taxes on the wealthy, as a campaign message.
positions.quote: We need to implement progressive taxation (raise taxes on the wealthy)

record.text: Championed the Retail Worker Safety Act, requiring panic buttons and violence-prevention plans for retail employees.
Championed the Roadway Excavation Quality Assurance Act, guaranteeing prevailing wages for infrastructure workers.
Secured passage of the New York State Fashion Workers Act, establishing basic labor protections for models and creatives.
Passed what her campaign calls the "Incorrigible Bill," removing offensive language from family and education law historically used to target girls of color.
Enacted the BIPOC Missing Women & Girls Task Force Bill, directing the state to address failures in missing-persons cases involving women of color.
Authored the NY HERO Act, establishing the first statewide airborne-infectious-disease workplace safety standard in the country.
Championed Abortion Shield Laws protecting doctors and patients, and a ban on toxic mercury in cosmetics.

Issued a joint statement with State Senator Andrew Gounardes calling for the full New York for All Act, opposing informal collusion between local agencies and ICE, following the state budget's ban on formal ICE agreements.

candidates.researchNotes: Reyes completed a Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey in 2020, the most recent one on file (none for 2026); this file relies instead on her official Assembly biography and her campaign's own accomplishments/priorities pages for current information, since her sponsored-legislation table on Ballotpedia is rendered via JavaScript and was not accessible to this research tool.

candidates.name: Zenobia Merced-Bonilla

priorities.text: Animal welfare, mental health, clean and safe streets, and public transportation, citing sanitation, disorder, and subway safety conditions as key concerns.

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website or completed Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey was located for Merced-Bonilla. Background and priorities are drawn from her 2025 City Council candidacy and a Bronx.com report on a Bronx Conservative Party meeting reported on January 31, 2026, where she spoke about a State Senate District 34 campaign before she appeared on the ballot for this Assembly seat instead; no Assembly District 87-specific policy statements were found. No birthplace, education or employment information for her could be found in a loaded public source.

candidates.name: Zakir Choudhury

priorities.text: Financial accountability and transparency: responsible budgeting, greater transparency in state spending, and reducing waste so tax dollars directly benefit District 87 residents.
Education and youth opportunities: fair and reliable school funding and expanded after-school and youth development programs.
Affordable living: reducing cost-of-living pressures, supporting affordable housing, and addressing rising energy and utility costs.
Public safety and community health: community-based safety programs and expanded access to mental health services.
Small business and local economy: support for entrepreneurs, local job creation, and reduced regulatory burdens.

candidates.researchNotes: Choudhury has not completed a Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey and has no official record (Ballotpedia lists no prior office). His campaign website's "About" section contains placeholder text alongside genuine campaign content; only the material clearly specific to his candidacy (the "Vision for Change" issues page) was used here. Degrees and employer names appear only on voter-aggregator sites and were not used.

None of the three candidates has completed a 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey. Merced-Bonilla has no campaign website; a Bronx.com report on a Bronx Conservative Party meeting reported January 31, 2026 supplied her District Leader role and stated priorities (given there for a State Senate District 34 campaign she pursued before this Assembly race).
